source.note: Six lanes, named by the operator in his own words: 1 deal investigation, 2 board/dream team recruitment, 3 firm interviews, 4 financial institutions, 5 business sellers, 6 joint venture partners (non dream team). Pena's slides (1862 the eleven steps, 1586 the ordering) supply what happens inside each lane and are cited per card. No dates: cadence, output per run, and the one thing that caps the multiple.

statuses.waiting: Built, waiting on one thing you own
statuses.partial: Half live — some pieces proven, some not
statuses.yours: Yours — the bot cannot do this one for you

order.title: Perfect the five lanes
order.detail: Investigation, dream team, firm interviews, sellers, JV partners. Each runs on volume and reports real yield. Nothing gets cleverer until these five are boring.

order.title: Perfect the machinery
order.detail: Then the part underneath: single-flight locks, audit log, send governor, dead-letter retry, kill switch. Speed without these is just a bigger blast radius.

order.title: Make it recursive
order.detail: Then outcomes feed scoring, letters and vertical playbooks, so cycle 30 beats cycle 1 at the same cost.

workstreams.name: Deal investigation
workstreams.pena_says: 2. Investigate generalities · 3. Investigate specifics · 6. Investigate continues
workstreams.cite: slide 1862 — the eleven steps; on red flags: "Investigation is a search for red flags. How many? ONE."
workstreams.one_line: Generalities first, then specifics, then a written verdict — every figure stamped verified, inferred or assumed.
workstreams.bot_does: Converts a listing into a 7-field deal file, scores it on 10 QLA factors, runs the red-flag sweep and local intel pack, and refuses to advance a deal with a blocked money field.
workstreams.output_per_run: 43 listings → 43 deal files → 11 walker-ready, all scored. 32 blocked, each naming the field that's missing.
workstreams.ceiling: Disclosure quality. Most blocks are a single missing EBITDA — the unblock ask (T1.06) raises this ceiling; nothing else does.
workstreams.blocker: Red-flag sweep and lice-comb deep dive specified, not built
workstreams.next: Build the generality sweep first: one red flag ends a deal, so it belongs before the deep dive.

workstreams.name: Board and dream team recruitment
workstreams.pena_says: INDUSTRY & IDEA, PLUS ANCHOR CHAIRMAN IN 1ST 30 DAYS · REMAINING DREAM TEAM BOARD MEMBERS, INCLUDING LAWYER, ACCOUNTANT, INDUSTRY EXPERT (S)
workstreams.cite: slide 1586 for the order — chairman first, then the rest · slide 1025 "IV Creating your Dream Team"
workstreams.one_line: Chairman first, then board seats, then the professionals — all approached in one cycle instead of one at a time.
workstreams.bot_does: Defines each seat as a role spec, sources candidates who match it, verifies every address by MX, and renders one approach letter per firm — no invented credentials, no invented warmth.
workstreams.output_per_run: 31 verified advisors across four roles in one session, 31/31 MX-checked; 6 role-specific letters staged for one deal; 40+ chairman candidates per build once T2.02 is built.
workstreams.ceiling: Reply rate and credible supply — how many people worth asking exist in that vertical. Volume answers it: more waves, more candidates, never a faster email.
workstreams.blocker: Your email address + app password (GMAIL_ADDRESS, GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD) to send
workstreams.next: Send the first wave the moment mail is on; the court tracker then shows which seats are filled.

workstreams.name: Firm interviews
workstreams.pena_says: 7. Action plan — a. Get others obsessed · b. Walk your talk (never ever share doubt)
workstreams.cite: slide 1862 · not named as a step in the deck — this lane is yours, and it had zero coverage before today
workstreams.one_line: Every firm that answers gets the same five questions and the same scorecard, so the choice is comparable instead of conversational.
workstreams.bot_does: Classifies each reply, matches it to the deal, sends the fixed interview pack, scores answers on identical axes, and escalates only what genuinely needs your voice on a call.
workstreams.output_per_run: Nothing yet — no interview pack, no scorecard, no comparison exists. Replies are classified today (T5.02) but nothing structured is waiting for them.
workstreams.ceiling: The answers themselves, plus one call per firm. The bot can make the comparison rigorous; it cannot be the person the firm is deciding whether to trust.
workstreams.blocker: T2.13 interview pack and scorecard is new and unbuilt
workstreams.next: Write the five questions and the scoring axes — that is the whole lane, and it is a page of text plus a table.

workstreams.name: Financial institutions
workstreams.pena_says: FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS: BANKS, INSURANCE CO'S, PE, ETC, WARMED UP & READY 2 ACCEPT 1ST DEAL
workstreams.cite: slide 1586 — the day-90 gate, the only deadline the source attaches to money
workstreams.one_line: Banks, insurers and PE opened before the first LOI exists, so the offer is fundable when it is made.
workstreams.bot_does: Targets lenders, bankers, insurers and PE firms at deal size, verifies every address, and writes the ask that matters: what you lend against, what you require personally guaranteed.
workstreams.output_per_run: 6 verified lender targets including the regional development company that lends at this size — 6/6 MX-checked. Insurance and PE were named by the source and uncovered; T2.16 now exists.
workstreams.ceiling: Appetite at your deal size. Answered with breadth: more institutions opened, not a faster application.
workstreams.next: Record stated appetite per institution so the LOI knows its funding before it knows its price.

workstreams.name: Business sellers
workstreams.pena_says: 1. Identify the idea · 6. Investigate continues · "You must kiss a lot of frogs! Period!"
workstreams.one_line: Every listed business, every broker, every owner who might sell — two channels, and a follow-up ladder that stops on any reply.
workstreams.bot_does: Sweeps marketplaces and firm sites, normalises verticals, filters against the buy-box, renders seller and broker letters, drives contact forms in a real browser, then runs the cadence with a hard stop rule.
workstreams.output_per_run: 43 listings swept and specced; 17 brokers verified at one office; 10 approaches staged; one live form filled end to end (9 fields, screenshot kept).
workstreams.ceiling: Mailbox reputation and seller supply. The touch cap is the hard wall: one approach per domain per cycle, enforced in the ledger, or the domain dies.
workstreams.blocker: Sending waits on the email credentials; forms and paperwork run without them
workstreams.next: Rate limits, bounce handling and opt-out — the three things that keep a mailbox alive long enough to matter.

workstreams.name: Joint venture partners (non dream team)
workstreams.pena_says: Not in the deck as a lane — adjacency is your distinction, and it is the right one.
workstreams.cite: your definition · outside the board by design: a JV partner gains from the deal without sitting on your board
workstreams.one_line: Operators and owners who gain from your deal without being on your board: co-investment, supply, roll-up participation.
workstreams.bot_does: Nothing yet — zero tasks existed for this lane until today. Sourcing and approach reuse the court engine; the term sheet and reciprocity ledger are new (T2.15).
workstreams.output_per_run: Nothing. Two tasks now exist (T2.14, T2.15); neither is built.
workstreams.ceiling: What the partner gets. A JV approach only works when the gain is specific and stated up front — vagueness reads as a favour request.
workstreams.blocker: New lane — T2.14 and T2.15 created today
workstreams.next: Define what a JV partner gains in this vertical, then clone the court approach path onto it.

workstreams.name: The engine room — not a front-end lane
workstreams.pena_says: Not in the source. This is the machine that runs the five, and it is labelled as ours.
workstreams.one_line: It runs the lanes on repeat, computes how much outbound makes waiting irrelevant, refuses to spend money, and keeps a log.
workstreams.bot_does: Schedules cycles, gates credentials, stamps provenance, computes the send plan under Little's Law, and (once built) holds locks, audit log, dead-letter retry and kill switch.
workstreams.output_per_run: A cycle that wakes, sweeps, stages, reads and reports — plus the arithmetic that turns a reply target into sends/day, messages in flight and prospects needed.
workstreams.ceiling: Deliverability. Per-mailbox caps are the only thing that can turn volume into a dead domain — the governor (T0.11) exists so the multiple is spent where it survives.
workstreams.blocker: Locks, audit log, dead-letter and kill switch specified, not built
workstreams.next: Single-flight lock and audit log first: they are what make a high-volume run trustworthy unattended.
